introduction.definition: A liquid–liquid coalescer removes fine droplets of one liquid from another — for example water from jet fuel or diesel. The fluid passes through coalescing cartridges whose fibres catch tiny droplets and merge them into large drops; these settle quickly into the water boot, from which an interface controller drains the water.
applications: Aviation fuel and diesel water removal
key_points: Turns small droplets into large drops
Interface level control on the boot

introduction.summary: A liquid–liquid coalescer removes fine water droplets from hydrocarbons (or oil from water). The fluid passes through coalescing cartridges whose fibres capture small droplets and merge them into large drops; a vane pack catches remaining drops, and the separated water settles into the boot where an interface controller drains it.

pressure.title: Coalescence: small drops become large drops
pressure.description: Fine dispersed droplets (a few µm to tens of µm) are captured by the fibres of the coalescing media, merge with other captured droplets and leave the outer surface as large drops. Large drops settle quickly (Stokes: velocity ∝ d²) into the water boot. Surfactants can disarm coalescing media, so they are selected for the interfacial tension of the system.

video_tutorials.title: Coalescer — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Coalescer.
A liquid–liquid coalescer removes fine droplets of one liquid from another — for example water from jet fuel or diesel.

The fluid passes through coalescing cartridges whose fibres catch tiny droplets and merge them into large drops; these settle quickly into the water boot, from which an interface controller drains the water.
Typical applications include aviation fuel and diesel water removal; water removal from LPG/condensates; oil removal from water (reverse configuration).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Coalescer works.
Fluid with dispersed water enters the vessel.
It flows through the coalescing cartridges.
Droplets grow and fall out of the flow.
The vane pack catches remaining drops.
Water collects in the boot and is drained.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Coalescer.
Drain/check boot interface; ΔP.
Sample outlet water content.
Replace coalescer elements.
Watch for media disarming: water passes through. Common cause: surfactants.
Watch for high δp: flow restriction. Common cause: particulates.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
